name: HeyLinks
tagline: AI-assisted link building: finds prospects, drafts pitches, and chases backlinks for your site.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The software half of link building is genuinely trivial: a prospect list, a scoring column, a mail merge, a status kanban. The part people actually pay for is the supply side, meaning site relationships, placement inventory, editor contacts, and a track record that gets a reply instead of a spam label. An agent can build you a competent prospecting and outreach cockpit in an afternoon, and then you sit there sending cold emails to strangers who ignore you. There is also a deliverability tax: cold outreach at volume from a fresh domain is its own miserable discipline involving warmup, SPF, DKIM, and a lot of bounce babysitting. Build the tracker, do not expect the links.
coreLoopDIY: A local app that pulls link prospects from search and competitor backlink exports, scores them, drafts personalized pitches with an LLM, and tracks each thread through a pipeline.
requirements: A search API key (Serper, Brave, or similar) for prospecting
A backlink data source, which usually means an existing Ahrefs or Semrush export or subscription
An email account with SMTP access, plus SPF and DKIM configured if you send at any volume
whatYouLose: Any actual link supply: no publisher relationships, no placement inventory, no editors who recognize the sender
Backlink index data, which is the expensive part and which nobody gives away
Managed deliverability: warmup, rotation, bounce handling, and reputation monitoring are yours now
Whatever quality filtering keeps you off link farms and out of a manual action
Reporting a client will accept without asking who built the spreadsheet
moatNotes: Two separate moats stacked: a crawled backlink index nobody can cheaply reproduce, and a rolodex of sites that will actually publish.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the deliverable is a link on someone else's website, and no amount of local tooling makes a stranger's editor say yes. Paid link building services are really buying access: pre-negotiated placements, a warmed sending infrastructure, and an index of who links to whom. A self-built cockpit gets you organized, and organized cold outreach with no relationships still converts at a rate that makes you question the whole exercise. People pay to skip the six months of relationship building, or to hand the reputational risk to someone else.
notes: The outreach cockpit is a weekend build; the links are not. The moat is a crawled backlink index plus a list of sites that will actually hit publish.
prompt:
Build a local link building cockpit called "linkdesk". Single user, runs on my machine, no accounts, no hosted backend.

Stack, no substitutions: Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, Tailwind, shadcn/ui. Everything in one repo, `npm run dev` starts it.

Data model:
- prospects: id, domain, url, page_title, discovered_via, topic, contact_name, contact_email, relevance_score (0-100), notes, status enum (new, queued, sent, replied, won, dead), created_at.
- outreach: id, prospect_id, subject, body, sent_at, channel, thread_notes.
- campaigns: id, name, target_url, anchor_ideas (text), pitch_angle (text).

Features, in scope:
1. Prospecting: a form where I enter a keyword or a competitor domain. Query a search API (Serper, key in .env as SERPER_API_KEY) for patterns like "keyword + resources", "keyword + write for us", "keyword + roundup". Dedupe by registrable domain against existing prospects. Insert as status=new.
2. CSV import: accept Ahrefs or Semrush backlink exports. Let me map columns in the UI, then import as prospects. This is the main data path, treat it as first class.
3. Enrichment: for a selected prospect, fetch the page server side, extract title, meta description, and any mailto or /contact link. Store what you find. Respect robots.txt, one request at a time, 2 second delay, honest user agent.
4. Scoring: an LLM call (OpenAI, OPENAI_API_KEY in .env) that reads page title plus extracted text and returns relevance_score and a one line reason for the active campaign. Show the reason in the table.
5. Pitch drafting: generate a short personalized email per prospect using the campaign pitch_angle and the enriched page context. Editable in a textarea before anything is saved.
6. Pipeline: kanban board by status, drag to move, click a card for the full thread.
7. Sending: optional. If SMTP_* vars exist in .env, a send button that fires one email via nodemailer and logs it. No bulk send, no scheduling, no tracking pixels. One at a time, on purpose.
8. Dashboard: counts by status, reply rate, won links with live link checking (fetch the target page, confirm my URL still appears).

Out of scope, do not build: multi user auth, a backlink crawler of my own, email warmup, inbox sync, proxy rotation, anything that scrapes Google HTML directly.

Secrets in .env.example only. Ship a seed script with 15 fake prospects so the UI is not empty. README: setup, which env vars are optional, and a blunt paragraph saying this tool organizes outreach and does not create link supply.
